Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
Columbus Ohio--in a mad and violent struggle, fraught with revolting Anarchs,
decapitations, charming socialites, and a Garou biker gang, two clans emerged
from the fray victorious: the Settites and the Tremere.

This year at Origins '99, WOTC sponsored three VTES tournaments, two
constructed and a sealed, indicating increased support from WOTC, as for the
last few years WOTC only ran one or two VTES events per year. Scott Larabee of
WOTC was very enthusiastic about continuing VTES support, discussing both the
upcoming World's Championship at Gencon and the mini expansion to be released
this fall. While there were not actually any judges available to run the VTES
events, Peter Bakija (that's me) stepped in to run both constructed events.

The Thursday constructed tournament had a strong turn out of 16 players
competeing in three rounds of preliminaries and a 5 player final. Going into
the finals were:

Jay Kristoff (11 vps) playing a speedy little Ventrue based weenie Presence
vote/bleed deck.

Howard Sanders (6 vps and last years Origins champion) playing his tradmarked
Protean/Dominate/Obfuscate stealth and bleed deck.

Joshua Duffin (5 vps) playing a tight, industry standard, Brujah Immortal
Grapple Rush deck.

David Raynor (4 vps) playing a Tremere Muaziz based Stealth and Bleed deck.

David McCarty (4 vps) playing a rude and efficient Settite corruption deck.

Also with 4 vps going in to the finals were Peter Bakija's Nosferatu IG Rush
deck and Steve Marbit's Toreador Anson based vote deck, but they lost out on
the tie breaker points.

The seating of the final, in order, was Howard, Josh, McCarty, Kristoff,
Raynor. Early in the game, Josh suffered from horrible hand jam, being
completely unable to draw a Rush action. As a result, he gets bled to one by
Howard very quickly. On his last turn, Josh managed to finally draw a Bum's
Rush, and in a flurry of ultraviolence, Josh managed to torporize Howard's
Caitlin. Josh is then ousted before his 6th turn, giving Howard 1 vp.
Meanwhile, McCarty had stolen 2 or 3 of Kristoff's little vampires and was
keeping quite a bit of pressure on him. Raynor soon loses half of his 10 pool
to win the Hostile Takeover bid for his Muaziz, but breaks even as he managed
to Grave Rob Howard's Caitlin soon after. Kristoff is the next to fall, at the
hands of his own Anarch Revolts (leaving Howard at 2 vps). The three way game
quickly becomes critically unstable when McCarty steals the highly fickle
Caitlin from Raynor with a Form of Corruption, using her to oust Raynor
(McCarty gains 1 vp). In the very end, with Howard at 2 pool and McCarty at 3
pool, Howard goes to Govern McCarty for 3 bleed while McCarty still had a
blocker, in a desperate a hopeful attempt to top deck a stealth card. When
Howard draws a master card instead of a Lost in Crowds, Howard resigned.

First Place with 3 vps: Dave McCarty
Second Place with 2 vps: Howard Sanders

The Saturday constructed event had a smaller turnout, with only 10 players, but
still was a great time. After the three rounds of preliminaries, the top 5
scores were:

Peter Bakija (8 vps) playing an all Protean Form of Mist weenie bleed and Garou
biker gang deck.

Howard Sanders (6 vps) playing his Protean/Dominate/Obfuscate deck.

Dave Preston (5 vps) playing a wennie Presence bleed Anarch Revolt deck.

Jonathan who's last name I lost (sorry!) (4 vps) playing a weenie Anarch Revolt
vote deck.

Josh Duffin (3 vps) playing a Tremere Cryptic Mission/Society of Leopold deck.

The seating of the final, in order, was Josh, Peter, Howard, Dave, Jonathan.
Dave is quickly ousted by the combination Howards Stealth and Bleed deck and
Anarch Revolts, giving Howard 1 vp. Jonathan, who had been pretty much kept
down to this point, managed to pull off a Dramatic Upheaval, switching himself
with Peter (making Peter Howards prey and Jonathan Josh's prey). Then, just to
add spice, Jonathan throws a Millicent Smith in to the fray. Josh soon ousts
Jonathan (giving Josh 1 vp). The three way game stabilizes with Peter keeping
Howard at bay with constant pool gain (Blood Dolls and Eco Terrorists) and
attacking with his Garou, while Josh slowly bled Howard down. Howard's DiDi
Myers then got burned by Millicent Smith after Chandler Hungerford intercepts
her hunting on his Sport Bike. In a last attempt to oust Josh, Peter sends
Chandler to Computer Hack him out of the game, but is played like a puppet when
Jing Wei Deflects him to Howard, who has Greggor Andersen Redirect him back to
Josh, who then Wakes Jing Wei and has her Deflect Chandler back to Howard.
Howard is then ousted, and Chandler feels like a stooge, giving Josh 2 vps.
Josh then quickly destroys most of Peter's vampires with the combination of
Cryptic Mission and Society of Leopold, and ousts him, giving Josh 4 vps.

First Place with 4 vps: Josh Duffin
Second Place with 1 vp: Howard Sanders

All players involved were great fun and had an excellent time. Thanks to WOTC
for prizes and support and Scott Larabee for not canceling the events due to a
lack of judges.

Peter D Bakija
PD...@aol.com

"Can't find the spoon that we once had,
the sugar cubes will melt no more"
-Cibo Matto

Messages.Author: carlos_...@my-deja.com
Messages.Body:
> This year at Origins '99, WOTC sponsored three VTES tournaments, two

Larabee of

both the
> upcoming World's Championship at Gencon and the mini expansion to be
released
> this fall.

This leads to two questions:

1. Are there any concrete details yet for the mini-expansion? Is it
still in development process????

2. World Championship for VTES? WTF??????? I mean, it's nice that WotC
has renewed support, but this is a bit ludicrous (sp?). I assume that
there will be few (if any) players not from the US attending at this
year's Gencon, so calling it a World Championships is crap. Moreso as
it was never announced in any medium (apart perhaps from private
mails). I don't like the idea of having a World Championship played on
3 to 4 tables (max), almost no-one noticing what's going on, no
publicity, etc. IMO, there will be no more than 30 players in this
"World Championship". Did anyone inform all the VTES players in the
world? Was it in the Fragment of the Book of Nod announced? No? Hm.

> While there were not actually any judges available to run the VTES
> events, Peter Bakija (that's me) stepped in to run both constructed
> events.

No judges???? What's going on there in the US?

>
> The Thursday constructed tournament had a strong turn out of 16
players
> competeing in three rounds of preliminaries and a 5 player final.

Huh, a strong turnout you say. A medium turnout would be over 20
players in a constructed, like last weekend in Antediluvian Awakening,
Kosice. I think we have been 25 players.
For Draft, I turnout of 27 players is strong, as has been in March in
PS:Vienna II. :)

> David McCarty (4 vps) playing a rude and efficient Settite corruption
deck.

What about all the others, saying that Setites are not good in
tournaments?

> The Saturday constructed event had a smaller turnout, with only 10
> players,

10 players only???????? [shaking head] What's going on there? I suppose
it's power gamers with degenerate decks making tournaments
uninteresting for the majority. Perhaps 4CL makes for more diversitive
deck concepts... (don't get me wrong, this is not a move for 4CL)

> All players involved were great fun and had an excellent time. Thanks
to WOTC
> for prizes and support and Scott Larabee for not canceling the events
due to a
> lack of judges.

IMO, a tournament who doesn't have a judge is *very* badly organized.
Anybody similar experiences?

Would you care to give more details on this WC thing?

Carl
(VEKN Prince of Vienna)

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
Carl wrote:
>>1. Are there any concrete details yet for the mini-expansion? Is it still in
development process????>>

Not that I am aware of. They just were very defenite about producing it. The
distribution method is up in the air, and the cards involved are not yet
concrete, but they are making it by the end of the year.

>>2. World Championship for VTES? WTF??????? I mean, it's nice that WotC has
renewed support, but this is a bit ludicrous (sp?). I assume that there will be
few (if any) players not from the US attending at this year's Gencon, so
calling it a World Championships is crap.>>

Dude. Take a deep breath. Relax. It may very well be the National
Championships, and not the World Championships, but either way, it isn't like
it is a tournament on the Magic level. There are no "Qualifiers" or entrance
requirements, nor is there a substantial (if any) cash prize. It is being
called the X Championships just cause it is fun to do so. I suspect that if
there are more than 30 players, it will be a miracle.

>>No judges???? What's going on there in the US?>>

What is going on is that WOTC is supporting a game that hasn't beeb printed in,
like, 4 years. They commited to running three tournaments at Origins (which is
a huge annual convention with multiple thousands of attendees--second in size
only to Gencon), which was great, but never managed to find judges, as not all
that many people in WOTC are capable of running such an event. Thus, rather
than canceling the events, they hoped that someone would show up who was
willing to judge and play at the same time (with a 3 player triumverate of
judges in case of having to judge the judge). Luckily, I was there and willing
to do it. I fail to see the problem. They gave us tons of prizes, and as I was
running the show, I knew that we were playing with all the appropriate rules
and errata.

>>Huh, a strong turnout you say. A medium turnout would be over 20 players in a
constructed, like last weekend in Antediluvian Awakening, Kosice. I think we
have been 25 players.
For Draft, I turnout of 27 players is strong, as has been in March in PS:Vienna
II. :)>>

Boy, do you lead a special life. What do you gain here by critisizing the turn
out? I felt 16 players was great.

>>What about all the others, saying that Setites are not good in
tournaments?>>

I don't know what to make of this statement.

>>10 players only???????? [shaking head] What's going on there? I suppose it's
power gamers with degenerate decks making tournaments uninteresting for the
majority. Perhaps 4CL makes for more diversitive deck concepts... (don't get me
wrong, this is not a move for 4CL)>>

No, it is that Jyhad isn't all that widespread, as it is essentially a dead
game. The fact that we had about 30 players show up and have a great time in
the three different events works for me. The smallish turnout has nothing to do
with the rules, I assure you. It has to do with the fact that Jyhad has not
printed a card for 4 years and that there was a second large convention
(DragonCon) in Atlanta the same weekend with large Jyhad events (I believe that
LSJ was running them). The fact that we were there, having a good time, and
running a tournament, on the other hand, convinces WOTC that people still like
their game, regardless of the size.

>>IMO, a tournament who doesn't have a judge is *very* badly organized. Anybody
similar experiences?>>

Again, they were committed to running the events, but didn't have any qualified
judges. Would you rather they not run the events?

Yea!

My review of the events.
and all of the comments may be wrong or incorrect as time and fatigue have
blurred the memory.

Thursday, I arrived at Origins about 10 minutes late, but Peter was kind
enough to let me jump in.

Round one had me working hard to get my VPs. and Only took 1, the next game
I was quickly reduced to a road block with an effective vote deck.

Round 3 My deck took off ousting 3 people and was the last at the table.

The final round was yet another massive sweep for the settites taking 4VPs
and not 3 as peter claimed.

On that point I am quite sure, since I recall thinking that I had managed to
average the magical 2VP average for the 4 games.

Friday. Sealed deck, no Judge and 3 people who had no Idea that errata was
ever published.

Ended up taking several backward bleeds, but managed to seize 3 VP anyway.
The other players simple split the prizes and called it a day after 1 game.
:(

And to think I spend 15$ for that.

Friday, well I lost, but not by too much. I had 3 VPs going into the final
round, which tied me with another player. I missed out by 12 Tournament
points and ended sitting out.

Had the misfortune of not contesting a vampire in game 1, which lead to that
vampire massively bleeding my Predator, who in desperation did a Kindred
restructured and switch seats with me, Then I got to play speed bump. Ouch!

Over all I will say that the gamesmanship was very good, the players seemed
aware of the changes and everyone had a good time.

Raille
I could have been a contender.

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
Raille wrote:
>>The final round was yet another massive sweep for the settites taking 4VPs
and not 3 as peter claimed.

On that point I am quite sure, since I recall thinking that I had managed to
average the magical 2VP average for the 4 games.>>

Yeah, your right. Howard got 1 and you got 4. Sorry. Teach me to write the
tourney report after driving for 10 hours :-)

Anyway, a brief recount of my game experiences:

In the first tourney, I played my favorite--The Nosferatu Hate You, and did
very well, until my strategic error in game three.

Game 1, I got 3 VPs. I don't remeber who I killed, but I pretty much controlled
the table, but couldn't oust my prey fast enough to keep him from getting a
second VP. I did get some good use out of the Fame I put in my deck--I ousted
my prey by Faming his vamp, whacking her, and the 3 pool loss killed him.

Game 2, I got 1 VP. The game had me and James Hamblin's "The Brujah Kill, Kill,
Kill you" Rush deck as my grand prey. I ousted my prey for a VP, he ousted his
prey for a VP, and then the three way game (with James as my prey...) rapidly
degenerated into the two of us mangling each other (I think I got 5 vampires
burned/diablerized...), while the woman in seat three managed to pick up the
pieces of what was left and scored 3 VPs. I did manage to get even more use out
of my Fame, as I made James's Dre into a celebrity, sent him to torpor, and
then the next turn pulled him out and sent him in again. James then diablerized
his own Dre on his next turn, just to avoid further humiliation.

Game 3 saw me killed by my own madness. I was Howards S+B prey, and was keeping
him down pretty well, and again, James's predator, and as such, keeping the
heat off of him (I didn't want this game to fall into the same position as the
last one with me and James...). I was in a very good position and doing well in
the long term, slowly bleeding James while keeping Howard down, until I noticed
that the guy across the table's Toreador Anson Pool Gain deck was getting out
of control. While cleaning KoKo, he accidentally went off, and I cross table
Rushed Anson and decapitated him. The Toreador guy was none too pleased, and on
his next turn, Paritiy shifted 5 pool away from me, which allowed Howard to
just barely oust me. Doh. Before that, I was in a strong position with a lot of
pool and a tacit peace with James. After, I was dead.

Going into the finals, there was a 4 way tie for the last 2 seats (probably due
to me not doing the Tourney Points correctly, which I fixed on the second
tourney), so after a great deal of debate on what to do, we ended up simply
rolling dice for the seats. Me and the Toreador guy lost.

In the second tourney, I played my weenie Pro Form of Mist/Computer
Hacking/Garou deck (which I posted fairly recently), which did really well,
getting 8 VPs in the first 3 games. My Form of Mist bleeds were surprisingly
effective, and my Garou on Hawgs were wreaking havok (I never got the RPG on my
Garou with Hawg, sadly...) and then I got whacked in the final due to my good
seating getting moved by a Dramatic Upheaval, getting put in a bad spot, and
having to make a deal with Josh (to keep his Cryptic Missions from killing my
Garou and keeping down my weenies). In the end, when he had 2 pool which I
could have easily bled him out of, I neglected to due to A) Not really paying
attention and B) being too much a man of my word. As such, Josh eventually
killed me.

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
Carl wrote:
>>I know that there are no qualifiers or something else. But just calling it X
Championships doesn't make any sense, if it's not official. I wouldn't mind you
calling it "Crusade US" or something like that, but national or even world CS?
Better not.>>

I'm not calling it anything--I have nothing to do with any of this. I don't
work for WOTC, I'm not affiliated with WOTC in any way, and I'm not running the
event. I'm just reporting what I heard, and it is possible that me calling it
"World Championshp" was an error on my part (he could have called it "National
Championship". It is all a blur to me now...)

>>Yes, it's laughable IMO, too. And yes, the support from WotC is cool. But is
the name "World Championship" official? I mean, did WotC give it's consent to
use it officially? That's the big question.>>

I honestly don't know what they are calling it. I know that they are having a
"big" tourney at Gencon, and the winner gets their picture on a card in the new
set (i.e. they get to be a vampire), and the WOTC guy I was talking to called
it either the National Championships or the World Championships--I don't
remember which. Either way, it is just a vanity title, as the field is not
going to be made up of "reigonal" champions or invited masters, or anything of
the sort. It is just a tourney they hope will be big, and has a cool prize (get
to be on a card).

In the end, I suspect that it has a "big" name in hopes of attracting players,
and as Gencon is the biggest annual con in North America (12-15 thousand
people?), but having it there, they are most likely to get a good turnout. By
making a big deal of it (giving it a "big" name), the increase their turnout.

For the numbers to ratio like that, you'd need a larger number of Jyhad
players in the US which proportionates with its increased area. We're
fanatics over here, but there aren't _that_ many of us. ;-)There probably

because its one of the greatest problems with Jyhad in the US;
communicating with and even just finding others who play, then taking the

Hey. If I found anyone within a reasonable distance, I wouldn't care what
language they spoke either (unless it was Esperanto, then I'd have to worry
;-) Besides, I'd expect _everyone_ to have a problem with my bastardized
version of the Queen's good English (nods to Legbiter ;-)...
Friendships abound in this game. We're all a sort of outcast society in
the gaming world, sustaining a game which everyone is trying so hard to
kill. It builds comraderie. And calluses.

<grin> I never took it that way, myself. It is tough for those not here to

compelled to try, though.
